events.title: Emperor Commodus is assassinated
events.description: Conspirators including his mistress Marcia and the praetorian prefect had the wrestler Narcissus strangle Commodus in his bath. The murder ushered in the turbulent Year of the Five Emperors.
events.html: Conspirators including his mistress Marcia and the praetorian prefect had the wrestler Narcissus strangle Commodus in his bath. The murder ushered in the turbulent Year of the Five Emperors.

events.title: Belisarius enters Syracuse in triumph after conquering Sicily
events.description: Having met Ostrogothic resistance only at Panormus, which fell after a quick siege, the Byzantine general Belisarius completed the conquest of Sicily and made a triumphal entry into Syracuse at the end of his consular year.
events.html: Having met Ostrogothic resistance only at Panormus, which fell after a quick siege, the Byzantine general Belisarius completed the conquest of Sicily and made a triumphal entry into Syracuse at the end of his consular year.

events.title: Ealdorman Æthelwulf defeats a Danish Viking army at Englefield
events.description: Æthelwulf, ealdorman of Berkshire, led a West Saxon force of 1,400 men to victory over a Danish Viking army at Englefield, near Reading. It was the first of a series of battles after the Danes invaded Wessex that month.

events.title: Henry V forces his father, Emperor Henry IV, to abdicate
events.description: At Ingelheim, Henry V, who had sided with his father's opponents among the imperial princes and the reform papacy in the Investiture Controversy, forced Emperor Henry IV to abdicate. He then ruled for five years in agreement with the princes.
events.html: At Ingelheim, Henry V, who had sided with his father's opponents among the imperial princes and the reform papacy in the Investiture Controversy, forced Emperor Henry IV to abdicate. He then ruled for five years in agreement with the princes.

events.title: Elizabeth I charters the East India Company
events.description: Elizabeth I granted a monopoly of English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope to a company of London merchants. The East India Company eventually ruled much of India until 1858.
events.html: Elizabeth I granted a monopoly of English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope to a company of London merchants. The East India Company eventually ruled much of India until 1858.

events.title: Edison gives a public demonstration of electric lighting
events.description: Thomas Edison lit his Menlo Park laboratory and nearby streets with incandescent lamps for crowds who came by special train. The display showed electric light could be a practical system.
events.html: Thomas Edison lit his Menlo Park laboratory and nearby streets with incandescent lamps for crowds who came by special train. The display showed electric light could be a practical system.

events.title: Truman proclaims the end of hostilities in the Second World War
events.description: President Truman formally proclaimed the cessation of hostilities, more than a year after Japan's surrender. The legal state of war with Germany and Japan ended later, with peace treaties.
events.html: President Truman formally proclaimed the cessation of hostilities, more than a year after Japan's surrender. The legal state of war with Germany and Japan ended later, with peace treaties.

events.title: The last Soviet institutions cease to function
events.description: By the end of the year, all remaining institutions of the Soviet Union had ceased to operate, days after Gorbachev's resignation. Fifteen independent states took its place.
events.html: By the end of the year, all remaining institutions of the Soviet Union had ceased to operate, days after Gorbachev's resignation. Fifteen independent states took its place.

events.title: Boris Yeltsin resigns and hands power to Vladimir Putin
events.description: In a New Year's Eve television address, Boris Yeltsin unexpectedly resigned as president of Russia. Prime Minister Vladimir Putin became acting president and won election in March 2000.
events.html: In a New Year's Eve television address, Boris Yeltsin unexpectedly resigned as president of Russia. Prime Minister Vladimir Putin became acting president and won election in March 2000.
